background_story: Marshall was a brilliant and eccentric scientist who spent most of his life studying the works of Luigi Galvani, the 18th-century Italian physician who pioneered the field of bioelectricity. Fascinated by Galvani's discovery of the role of electricity in the human body, Marshall dedicated himself to furthering the research. He spent years experimenting with the concept of galvanism, attempting to harness its power to create innovative medical treatments. Marshall's colleagues often referred to him as 'the modern Galvani' due to his groundbreaking work. His tireless efforts eventually led to the development of a revolutionary new therapy that used electrical impulses to treat paralysis. Marshall's work not only changed the lives of countless individuals but also cemented his place in the annals of scientific history alongside his idol, Galvani.
